name: /e/OS
summary: A privacy-focused mobile operating system forked from LineageOS and AOSP, providing an ungoogled Android environment integrated with microG, BlissLauncher, App Lounge with privacy scores, and optional Murena Cloud services.
license: GPLv2 (Linux kernel) / Apache License 2.0 (AOSP userspace) & GPLv3/AGPL (associated services and apps)

content.introduction: /e/OS is a free and open-source mobile operating system focused on user privacy and de-Googling. Founded in 2017 by Gaël Duval and maintained by the non-profit e Foundation alongside its commercial partner Murena, /e/OS provides an alternative smartphone environment designed to prevent unwanted data collection while maintaining compatibility with the mainstream Android mobile ecosystem.
content.what_is_it: /e/OS is a turnkey mobile distribution derived from LineageOS and the Android Open Source Project (AOSP). It eliminates Google telemetry, default Google cloud integrations, and proprietary background trackers, replacing them with open-source system applications, microG compatibility libraries, and optional sovereign cloud storage integration.
content.aosp_lineageos_heritage_and_degoogling: Developed by Gaël Duval and the /e/ Foundation (Murena), /e/OS builds upon LineageOS device trees and foundational AOSP code while executing a systematic de-Googling process. The development team removes all hardcoded Google dependencies from the operating system: default DNS lookups, Network Time Protocol (NTP) servers, assisted GPS (SUPL) servers, and captive portal network detection probes are redirected from Google servers to privacy-respecting community infrastructure. To maintain high application compatibility for general consumers, /e/OS embeds microG by default, providing open-source implementations of Google APIs for push notifications (GCM/FCM) and location triangulation without establishing persistent Google account bindings.
content.interface_and_application_ecosystem: The user experience of /e/OS is centered on BlissLauncher, a clean graphical desktop interface that arranges application icons and widgets across unified home screens in a streamlined, accessible layout. Application discovery and software management are handled by App Lounge, a custom app repository that evaluates applications with a Privacy Score from 0 to 10 based on Exodus Privacy trackers and permission audits. App Lounge consolidates software from F-Droid, CleanAPK, and an unprivileged anonymous gateway to the Google Play Store, allowing users to install mainstream commercial apps without signing into a personal Google account.
content.privacy_controls_and_cloud_integration: A hallmark feature of /e/OS is Advanced Privacy, a dedicated system utility and home screen widget providing real-time oversight over data collection. Advanced Privacy allows users to spoof their geographical GPS location to arbitrary coordinates, mask their real public IP address via Tor or a Murena VPN proxy, and intercept tracking scripts embedded within installed applications, providing detailed weekly statistics on blocked tracking requests. The operating system is closely paired with Murena Cloud, an open-source online workspace powered by Nextcloud that provides encrypted file storage, contact synchronization, calendar management, and `@e.email` email hosting, giving users an integrated personal cloud alternative to commercial big-tech ecosystems.
content.hardware_coverage_and_commercial_availab: /e/OS supports over two hundred smartphone models through community-maintained builds and officially verified releases. The system is distributed both as downloadable ROM images for existing hardware (Samsung, Google Pixel, Xiaomi, Motorola) and preinstalled on commercial hardware sold by Murena, including Fairphone devices and the Murena 2 smartphone, which features physical hardware privacy disconnect switches for cameras, microphones, and wireless connectivity.
content.installer_and_update_process: /e/OS can be installed with a browser-based Installer that runs in Chrome/Chromium and uses WebUSB; the earlier Easy Installer is deprecated and being phased out. Devices not covered by the Installer use a command-line procedure documented per device, which the project lists for over 200 models. The Installer checks anti-rollback protection before flashing and refuses a build whose security patch is older than the one already on the device; /e/OS ships monthly, so the next release carries an updated patch level. Updates on an installed system go through the Updater (Settings > System > Advanced > Updater): download, install, then reboot.
content.lineageos_base_android_versions_and_appl: The project documentation describes /e/OS as a fork of LineageOS, itself derived from AOSP, and states that builds cover more than 200 smartphone models. Android versions are split into two groups: official and community builds currently cover Android 12 through Android 16, while Android 7.x to 11 are listed as discontinued or legacy, without dedicated ROM maintainers and without the newer applications such as App Lounge and Advanced Privacy. Application distribution goes through App Lounge, a single installer fronting Google Play for commercial applications, F-Droid for open-source ones and progressive web apps, and assigning each application a privacy score computed from the trackers detected by Exodus Privacy. The bundled applications are AOSP and LineageOS components: DocumentsUI as file manager, the AOSP sound recorder, calculator and keyboard, and a fork of LineageOS Glimpse as gallery.
content.build_channels_and_release_eligibility: The device catalogue defines four publication channels. Builds tagged `official` have completed a full testing cycle and are presented as usable as a daily driver. Builds tagged `community` carry the most recent development code, are provided as best effort without any guarantee, and may include known and significant bugs. `unofficial` builds made by community members and `custom` builds modified by their authors are explicitly left at the user's own risk. Both the official and the community channels receive over-the-air updates. For each entry the catalogue also publishes the AOSP version, whether the bootloader is lockable, the build variant (`user` or `userdebug`), the Play Integrity level declared, whether the battery is removable, and whether the device is supported by the web installer.
content.device_catalog_composition: A count of the device table carried out on 18 October 2026 returns 25 rows marked `official` and 262 rows marked `community`. These rows enumerate builds rather than distinct models: a single device family can appear under several variants. The AOSP versions present range from Android 12 to Android 16. The brand filter lists 10.or, Asus, BQ, Essential, F(x)tec, Fairphone, Gigaset, Google, Lenovo, LG, Motorola, Murena, Nothing, Nubia, OnePlus, Razer, Realme, Samsung, SHIFT, Solana, Sony, Teracube, Volla, Vsmart, Xiaomi, ZTE and ZUK, for devices released between 2016 and 2026. Some rows link to a shop, in particular for Murena devices and for the sixth-generation Fairphone.
content.substitution_of_google_services_and_back: The project describes the removal of Google services as a set of named substitutions: the default search engine is replaced by Murena Find, Google services are replaced by microG, connectivity checks do not use Google servers, and neither Google's NTP servers nor its DNS servers are used. Geolocation relies on BeaconDB in addition to GPS. These substitutions operate at system-service level rather than inside individual applications: they cover search, notifications, network-based location and name resolution.
content.ecosystem_layers_and_system_components: The project describes /e/OS as a mobile ecosystem rather than a bare ROM, and enumerates the components it ships: an installable operating system for smartphones, forked from LineageOS and AOSP and stripped of Google code; a default set of open source applications adapted for the system; a group of online services tied to the operating system, namely a meta search engine, a cloud drive with data synchronisation, mail, calendar, notes and tasks; Advanced Privacy, which acts on application trackers and advertising; and Parental Control, which filters applications and web content for children. The same page dates the project's launch to the end of 2017 and presents it as the first mobile system built around deGoogling, a claim the project makes about its own history rather than an independently established fact.
advantages: Turnkey privacy-by-default mobile environment eliminating Google tracking and invasive telemetry
App Lounge unifies F-Droid, PWAs, and Google Play with integrated Exodus Privacy tracker scores
Advanced Privacy system utility provides in-app tracker blocking, IP masking, and location spoofing
Native microG integration preserves functionality for apps requiring push notifications and maps
Broad hardware support spanning over 200 device models, with preinstalled commercial hardware options
disadvantages: BlissLauncher interface lacks a traditional application drawer, which may diverge from standard Android habits
Certain high-security banking or DRM-protected apps requiring strict hardware attestation may fail
Updates on community-maintained device builds depend on volunteer maintainers and vary in frequency
who_is_it_for: Everyday smartphone users seeking an out-of-the-box de-Googled mobile operating system with app store access
Privacy advocates desiring transparent visibility into in-app tracking and granular network blocking
Buyers seeking preinstalled, privacy-respecting hardware supported by a dedicated commercial entity
who_is_it_not_for: Users requiring advanced kernel-level exploit mitigations and hardware memory tagging (MTE)
Users exclusively reliant on commercial Google Mobile Services accounts and proprietary Google apps
content.verdict: /e/OS provides an accessible, fully de-Googled mobile operating system that balances privacy protection with daily usability. By combining a LineageOS foundation with microG, App Lounge privacy metrics, and optional cloud sovereign services, it provides a functional consumer alternative to commercial Android distributions.

relations.name: LineageOS
relations.note: Upstream community Android distribution whose device trees, HAL adaptations, and codebase form the direct technical foundation of /e/OS.

relations.name: Android / AOSP
relations.note: Base foundational open-source mobile operating system stack from which /e/OS is downstream-derived.

relations.name: CalyxOS
relations.note: Alternative privacy-oriented Android distribution that also utilizes microG but focuses primarily on Google Pixel, Fairphone, and Motorola hardware.

relations.name: GrapheneOS
relations.note: Alternative hardened mobile operating system emphasizing defensive security mitigations on Google Pixel hardware.
